activity_context.topic_title: Computing Partial Derivatives Using the Rules of Differentiation

feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+{y}^{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+{y}^{5}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+{y}^{5}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) & =(\frac{∂}{∂x}(x)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x+x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x))+{y}^{5}\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =((1)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x+x\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡x))+{y}^{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x-x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{y}^{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =(1+{y}^{5})\operatorname{cos}⁡x-x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$
